page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled and peak clock speeds reaching 4.5 GHz. The hardware package integrates 512.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory-to-core ratio. The CPU topology features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by support for advanced vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16.

Benchmark results demonstrate high compute and memory capacity. Single-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, matched by a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 92,179.05 and strong multi-core throughput of 118,390.71. Memory subsystems sustain 203.18 GB/s in large-block read operations and 131.02 GB/s during large-block uncached writes, contributing to top-tier performance in database operation tests and 98.7 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves top-tier generation rates on small and medium language models, although throughput normalizes to mid-tier performance when executing large 70-billion parameter models.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, leaving disk persistence to external Azure Premium Storage attachments. With its high memory density and 64 dedicated compute threads, the E64as_v7 delivers qualitative resource efficiency for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, intensive data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E64as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores, driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz. Backed by 512.0 GB of total RAM, it provides 8.0 GB of memory per core. The underlying AMD processor features AVX-512 instruction sets, cryptographic acceleration, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Benchmarking confirms top-tier single-core performance and PassMark CPU ratings, supported by strong large-block memory read bandwidth of 203.18 GB/s. Redis SET evaluations exceed 98 million operations per second, while PassMark database operations place the instance in the top ten percent. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage volumes. This platform is technically suited for large in-memory caching, enterprise transactional databases, and complex data processing pipelines.
